items.html:
GPU appendix verified: 20/20 cases succeeded, following 9 passing real-device Rust tests. No reruns or source changes.

Against the fastest measured CPU alternative at 4 or 16 threads, using the 16-thread GPU round-trip measurements:

Workload Medium Large
Cached fields 7.21× 10.96×
Cached coefficient adjoint 4.67× 10.32×
Fused real-wave fields 4.14× 3.14×
Fused complex-wave fields 3.38× 3.05×

Tiny GPU cases were 6–32× slower. Cold setup materially changes the comparison: cached medium/large cases need approximately 440/14 repeated applications against the selected CPU configurations. The raw large-case “0 applications” estimate uses a different CPU layout; I flagged this for the report.

Maximum checked forward discrepancy: 2.09e−16; cached adjoint discrepancy: 1.48e−14; normalized Hermitian-pairing residual: 6.18e−17. Sampling errors are CPU/GPU envelopes. Logical buffers are recorded, not peak VRAM.

Hardware and source identities are consistent across cases: RTX 4080 SUPER, driver 610.57.04, Rust 1.94 release; one exact executable/source identity per example. CPU thread counts match their declared budgets.

Evidence: manifest, build and hardware checks.
